To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GWAS and cQTL approaches identified SNP markers associated with oil, protein and glucosinolate contents and hemicelluloses in a panel of winter oilseed rape genotypes.
the GWAS approach was successful in identifying SNP markers associated with glucosinolate and hemicelluloses content in a large association panel of winter oilseed rape.

(i) GWAS is an efficient tool for identifying SNP markers associated with oilseed rape seed quality traits, (ii) GWAS is a suitable alternative to traditional QTL mapping, (iii) the use of a large number of markers in a GWAS analysis increases the power to detect associations, and (iv) GWAS and cQTL analyses can be used together to increase the efficiency of association mapping studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of SNP markers associated with important seed quality traits in winter oilseed rape.
the development and validation of molecular marker-assisted selection (MAS) strategies in winter oilseed rape for seed glucosinate and seed hemicelulose content.
the use of AM to identify molecular markers for breeding purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GWAS is the most powerful approach for association mapping of quantitative traits in B. Napus.

the AM approach was more powerful in identifying SNP markers associated with glucosinolate and hemicelluloses contents in B. napu s, while the cQTL approach was more powerful for oil and protein contents.
AM is an efficient and powerful approach for the identification of molecular markers associated with complex traits in B. napus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AM can be a useful tool for identifying marker-trait associations in B. napushigher throughput and with a lower cost than QTL mapping.
the GWAS and cQTL approaches identified SNP markers that were consistently associated with seed quality QTL in the B. napu s panel.
the AM approach is a powerful tool to identify SNP markers that can be used to improve breeding efficiency for seed quality traits in oilseed rape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of AM in B. napusespecially with a GWAS approachis a powerful tool to identify marker-trait associations.
the cQTL approach can be used as an efficient alternative to GWAS, especially for traits that are controlled by a limited number of genes, and when a large number of SNP markers is not available.
GWAS and cQTL approaches can be used in combination in order to increase the power of AM studies.
